findings.title: canExchangeTo and other reachable methods now throw UnsupportedOperationException under V2.
findings.body: Before this change, `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` returned the V1 `ClientPermissions`, which handled `canExchangeTo`, `isPermissionsEnabled`, `getPermissions`, `setPermissionsEnabled` and `resource`. These now throw `UnsupportedOperationException`. Legacy token exchange calls `management(session, realm).clients().canExchangeTo(...)`, so with FGAP v2 enabled a token-exchange request would fail with a 500 instead of being allowed or denied. The client `management/permissions` admin endpoints would also return a 500 instead of a clean 4xx. The unused `getEvaluationContext` helper suggests the exchange path was started and not finished. Return a deny result (`false`) or a proper client error instead of throwing on these paths.

findings.title: Missing "Clients" type resource causes an NPE instead of a denial.
findings.body: If no per-client resource exists, `hasPermission(client, scope)` falls back to `getResourceTypeResource(..., CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE)` and never checks the result for null. The type resources are created when a realm's admin-permissions client is set up. A realm that enabled FGAP v2 before this change has only the "Users" type resource, so this call returns null. Then `findByResource(server, null)` or `resource.getScopes()` fails, and an admin without manage-clients gets a 500 on every client view or update instead of a 403. I could not check `getResourceTypeResource`, so it may create the resource on demand. If it does not, return `false` when `resource == null`, as the scope-less `hasPermission(String)` already does.
